results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response:
There are several types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain. These include alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which can be further subdivided into subtypes such as core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t, and claw-count classes. VFB places 7 direct subtypes under [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), with 22 subtypes in total across 2 levels. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx. VFB records show that there are [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body, including larval uniglomerular projection neurons and larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neurons.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
The [adult central brain](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047887 "Open adult central brain in Virtual Fly Brain") contains approximately 32,388 neurons, according to FlyWire reports. VFB has annotated [9413](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047887,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central brain") neuron types with some part in the adult central brain.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- ~32,388 neurons (Whole adult brain, both optic lobes and ocellar ganglia included. Ventral nerve cord NOT included; neurons crossing the neck connective are truncated at the brain boundary. Subcount: fully in central brain. One female adult. Dataset: FlyWire connectome neurons, v783.) — [Dorkenwald S et al. (2024) Nature 634(8032):124-138 — PMID 39358518](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07558-y "Open Dorkenwald S et al. (2024) Nature 634(8032):124-138 — PMID 39358518 via DOI (new tab)")

_FlyWire reports 32,388 neurons FULLY CONTAINED in the central brain out of 139,255 in the whole brain. Neurons that arborise in the central brain but also elsewhere are not in that subcount, so it is a lower bound on 'neurons in the central brain', not a census of them._

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

Reference: [How many neurons are in the fly brain?](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/docs/concepts/neuron-counts/ "Open “How many neurons are in the fly brain?” — Virtual Fly Brain documentation (new tab)")

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the Drosophila central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the three paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions such as navigation and orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal and memory-related behaviours. The answer uses the reading "[adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003632 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain")", but VFB also holds data under alternative names including anterior chiasma of the central complex, posterior chiasma of the central complex, central complex neuroblast, and [adult central complex on adult brain template JFRC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00030866 "Open adult central complex on adult brain template JFRC2 in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB holds [363](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003632,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central complex") records of neurons with some part in adult central complex and [362](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003632,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in adult central complex") records of neurons with synaptic terminals in adult central complex.

results.question: What genetic tools are commonly used to label mushroom body neurons in Drosophila?
results.response: The answer uses the reading of "[Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain")" as Kenyon cell, with alternative readings including adult lateral horn-mushroom body neuron 1, adult atypical mushroom body output neuron, adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron, and adult mushroom body modulatory input neuron. VFB records show genetic tools including PBac{544.SVS-1}Bsg[CPTI100062] and PBac{566.P.SVS-1}Bsg[CPTI100005] expression patterns are used to label Kenyon cell.

results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is a type of neuron with a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. It detects looming stimuli and elicits a jump escape response. In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. The LPLC2 neuron projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. There are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe and they are cholinergic.

The answer uses the reading of "[adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain")" as the main structure, with cell body rind of adult lateral horn as an alternative. results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. It has a distinct anatomy, with one cell per hemisphere, a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, and a large descending axon that is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective.

The giant fiber neuron connects to several downstream classes, with the strongest specific targets being [mesothoracic extracoxal trochanter depressor muscle motor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053153 "Open mesothoracic extracoxal trochanter depressor muscle motor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult efferent neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051964 "Open adult efferent neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [NB3-3 lineage primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048874 "Open NB3-3 lineage primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult IN18B034 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20010307 "Open adult IN18B034 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [peripherally synapsing interneuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007408 "Open peripherally synapsing interneuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult premotor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051437 "Open adult premotor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047106 "Open Notch ON hemilineage primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [adult IN06B008 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20009235 "Open adult IN06B008 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). The giant fiber neuron also connects to itself.

There are available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron, including [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") split-GAL4 combinations. Additionally, VFB records show [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") transgene expression reports for the giant fiber neuron, including expression patterns for P{GMR78G07-GAL4}, P{GMR79D08-GAL4}, and P{GMR91H05-GAL4}, among others. Relevant publications include Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), and Namiki et al. (2018).

An additional, much narrower, 9th layer, which lacks a columnar organization, sits dorsal to layer 8. The number of columns varies for different neuronal types.

turns.response: The [protocerebral bridge](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003668 "Open protocerebral bridge in Virtual Fly Brain") is a handle bar-shaped synaptic neuropil located just posterior to the fan-shaped body. Its lateral edge ends at the posterior end of the inferior clamp near the medial equatorial fascicle. A row of 18 connected slices, 9 on each side of the midline, forms a dorso-posteriorly located part of the central complex embedded in the cortex between the calyces of the two mushroom bodies.

results.question: How does the olfactory system work in flies?
results.response: The [olfactory system](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007688 "Open olfactory system in Virtual Fly Brain") in flies is an anatomical system that functions in the sensory perception of smell. It works through a feed-forward course of olfactory information from antenna and antennal lobe to mushroom body and lateral horn, with various neuron classes including antennal-lobe receptor neurons, antennal lobe local neurons, uniglomerular and multiglomerular projection neurons, Kenyon cells, MBONs, DANs, lateral horn neurons, and wedge projection neurons.
